Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-15T09:14:00Z
Subject: Borealis onboarding: request to enter gate + pin v2.1.x

Avery / infra / ML teams —

We have an inbound request from Borealis (see attached model card and the initial eval they sent). Product wants to evaluate Borealis-XL v2.1.2 for inclusion in the hosted catalog and to support it behind a pinned rollout for the launch of Document Q3 features. High-level asks:

- Can infra verify compatibility of v2.1.2 with our runtime (tokenizer, rotary/rope changes, KV cache memory profile for 2k+ context)?
- ML: can you run the usual perf + safety eval suite and report regressions vs. Sable-7B baseline (attached sample eval)?
- Ops: we need a proposed canary and pin window if we approve (suggested: 7d canary at 5% then 30d pin for stability).

Constraints: launch date target is 2027-05-01. Legal/procurement will need a procurement packet if we move forward. Please respond with gating checklist items and a rough timeline by EOD Tuesday 3/16.

Attachments: borealis_model_card.pdf, borealis_initial_eval.csv

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Model Catalog
Redwood Inference
From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, avery_johnson@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-16T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Borealis onboarding: request to enter gate + pin v2.1.x

Laura / team —

Quick infra readout after a brief local run with their provided artifacts (I pulled s3://vendor-uploads/borealis/v2.1.2/artifacts.tar.gz):

- Tokenizer: tokenization appears compatible with our byte-level tokenizer but there are differences in pretokenization for hyphenation which changes token counts on citational text by ~2-4%. We should add a tokenizer delta check to the intake pipeline.
- KV cache growth: v2.1.2 uses a denser KV layout; for 2k context we saw ~1.8x increase in KV memory vs our Sable baseline in the same sequence length distribution. That will affect max_concurrent for hosted instances.
- Attention kernels: model uses a rotary variant not in our fast-path kernels; I got a fallback kernel but P50 is ~1.3x higher. Need a kernel implementation or software fallback flag.

Ask from infra: we need the full ONNX/FTG exports and a reference input sequence set (their test set). Also recommend pinning to the vendor's v2.1.2 release (not v2.2-preview) during canary until we confirm kernel parity.

I attached a short kernel_report.txt with microbenchmarks.

--Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, avery_johnson@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-17T14:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Borealis onboarding: request to enter gate + pin v2.1.x

Team —

I ran the standard evals on the sample artifacts (seeded prompts + safety harness). Short summary:

- Quality: on general summarization and instruction-following, v2.1.2 is equal-or-better than Sable-7B. For math and multi-step chain-of-thought prompts we saw a small regression in exact-match answers (~3.5% lower).
- Safety: the safety suite flagged a slightly higher hallucination rate on finance prompts (not an outright safety fail but observable).
- Latency: my microbench matches Dev's numbers for CPU fallback; GPU runtimes are okay with a minor kernel mismatch.

Recommendation: allow onboarding but gate the model behind an ML quality check and telemetry. Pinning to v2.1.2 is fine, provided we instrument the following metrics for the canary: P50/P95 latency, token-cost delta, hallucination rate by eval-set, and inference error rates. Canary: 5% traffic, 7 days. If those metrics are stable, proceed to a 30-day pinned window where routing defaults to the pinned variant. Also suggest enabling an automatic fallback route to Borealis-XL-lite if latency or hallucination thresholds are crossed.

I'll prepare a checklist with the eval artifacts and expected thresholds by EOD Friday 3/19.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Applied ML, Model Onboarding
Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: dev_patel@redwood.ai, avery_johnson@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-19T09:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Borealis onboarding: request to enter gate + pin v2.1.x

Folks —

Thanks for the early triage. Two infra operations items that will determine whether we need a capacity carve-out:

1) If KV memory is +1.8x for typical DocQ distributions, we should not schedule this onto shared pools without reducing max_concurrent or offering an isolated GPU pool. I'd prefer a temporary dedicated pool for the canary to avoid tail latency impact.
2) We need an autoscale policy tweak for the canary: lower target_util to 45% and enable faster scale-up. Also, we should create a routing policy that pins traffic by customer tier during the 30d pin (e.g., start with internal customers + beta partners).

Timeline impact: creating a dedicated pool + updated autoscale policy is a 5–7 business day ops task. If we want the 5% canary by 2027-04-01, we need signed procurement and final artifacts by 2027-03-24.

--Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Borealis onboarding: entry gate + pin request (v2.1.x) — consolidated plan

Thanks everyone — consolidating next steps and owners so legal/procurement can kick off: 

Summary decisions:
- Approve controlled onboarding of Borealis-XL v2.1.2 for a 7-day, 5% canary, with an expected 30-day pinned stabilization window post-canary.
- Canary will run on a temporary dedicated pool to avoid noisy neighbor effects. Infra to provision pool and autoscale tweaks (Marcus / Dev).
- ML to publish the exact thresholds for hallucination, latency, and token-cost that will fail the canary (Priyom).
- Tokenizer delta check + ONNX exports required from vendor; procurement needs the artifact link & SOC2 attestation from Borealis.

Action items: 
- Laura: start procurement packet + vendor packet request (contract, SOC2, export artifacts).
- Sara (Borealis): please send ONNX/FTG exports, tokenizer config, and updated model_card with exact v2.1.2 hash.
- Marcus/Dev: infra carve-out timeline (ETA 5–7 business days once artifacts are available).
- Priyom: ML thresholds doc due EOD 3/19 (per earlier email) — please confirm if you need extra time.

Attachments: borealis_onboard_playbook.pdf (draft canary runbook).
Related HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HS-88762

I'll loop in procurement/legal after Laura confirms the initial packet. If anyone sees a blocker to the 2027-04-01 canary target, flag now.

Thanks —
Avery Johnson
